Fury and Fury X are essentially the same card, except the Fury X has an all-in-one water cooler for a $100 premium. The Fury is $550, and the Fury X is $650.

Based on the announced specs, the performance of the Fury is expected to be pretty close to, and probably a bit faster than, a 980 Ti, and it will come in $100 cheaper when comparing the air-cooled version to the air-cooled 980 Ti.

The Fury Nano was also announced. It sounds like a cut-down Fury chip with greater power efficiency (2x Performance per watt compared to 290X). The card is 6" long and is probably designed for small form factor builds. I'm pretty excited to see how good this one is.

The water-cooled Fury X comes out June 24th (8 days), and the air-cooled Fury comes out July 12th. The Nano comes out sometime this summer.

Edit: They also announced a dual-GPU version of the card, but there weren't a lot of details and it doesn't come out until the fall. I'm sure we'll get more details later.

When playing through Fallout, or any Bethesda game really, be sure to go off the beaten path. While the stories and most easily accessible quests are fun, I find most of the fun to be in the exploration. In dark corners of abandoned buildings, in places you never even thought of you'll find new places to see, new people to talk to, and more. Don't limit yourself to the path!
